subject: Starter subsidy eligibility — SparkStart cohort 4 (promo credits request)
messages:
From: Marc Reyes <marc@sparkstart.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Starter stipend — cohort 4 eligibility and extra credits

Hi Chloe,

Happy new year — hope you had a great break. We run SparkStart Labs (seed-stage accelerator) and are onboarding Cohort 4 in February. Historically Redwood provided a small starter stipend for each cohort company (pilot credits) to get them running. Our program has a few alumni companies that are rejoining for the new cohort and they fall just outside your 90-day new-signup window.

We wanted to check whether Redwood can make a one-off exception to extend the starter credits to these returning startups, and whether the credits can be carried forward to cover first-month spikes. Details: approx 12 companies, expected avg monthly spend per company $400–1,200, and a few will be in Canada (not US).

I attached a quick cohort membership list for context. Can we do a short call this week to align on terms? We’re flexible on structure but want to lock something before our kickoff (Feb 1).

Thanks,
Marc Reyes
Program Director — SparkStart Labs
marc@sparkstart.com
Attachment: cohort-membership.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>

Hi Marc — great to hear from you and congrats on Cohort 4.

Quick clarifying Qs before we jump on a call:
- Can you confirm how many of the 12 are returning alumni versus brand new startups?
- Estimated first 30-day total spend across cohort (so we can size a one-time top-up)?
- Any regulatory constraints for Canadian companies (we have slightly different terms for EU/CA regions)?

Our standard program covers new signups within 90 days; exceptions are possible but need approval from revenue ops and the partnerships lead. Looping in Aditya to weigh in on allowable top-ups and any cap requirements.

I can do a 20-min sync Fri Jan 9th 10:30am PT if that works — otherwise suggest times.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Starter stipend — cohort 4 eligibility and extra credits

Chloe — thanks for the ping and context. We’ve granted similar exceptions for a few accelerator partners last year; recommend the following one-off construct here:

Proposal (subject to ops sign-off):
- One-time credit top-up of $5,000 USD per returning company (applied as account credits).
- Credits expire 45 days from issuance to avoid long tail usage; exceptions for CA customers need legal review (we can extend to 60 days if SparkStart takes on a short attestation).
- Apply usage caps: per-company monthly cap $2,500 to limit exposure; any overage billed at standard rates.
- Credits applied via HubSpot deal (DEAL-2026-1374) and require a signed DocuSign for audit trail.

I attached our standard credit T&Cs and the HubSpot link. If SparkStart confirms count and agrees to the expiry, we can route this as a revenue ops exception and schedule delivery the week of Jan 12.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Revenue Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Credit_T&Cs.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2026-1374

Chloe / Aditya — thanks, this looks good. Confirming: 12 companies total, 4 returning alumni, 8 brand-new signups. Aggregate expected first-30 spend ~ $7,800.

We can accept the $5k top-up for returning companies and the $2,500 monthly cap. For administrative reasons some of our partners prefer a 60-day expiry window; would Redwood be willing to extend to 60 days for the 4 returning companies if we sign the DocuSign and provide the roster as a CSV?

I’ve started the DocuSign for the agreement (link below) — happy to sign once we have confirmation. We want credits in place by Jan 15 to include in onboarding docs.

Best,
Marc
